message.content: {"caption":"A four-panel chart compares methods by curated data size and shows reasoning performance across training steps in math, coding, and overall.","description":"The left panel, “Data Comparison,” lists AZR (Ours), Oat-Zero, SimpleRL-Zoo, ORZ, CodeR1, AceCoder, and PRIME-Zero vertically. Its horizontal “Curated Data Size” axis is logarithmic, with labeled ticks at 10⁻¹, 10¹, 10³, and 10⁵; the legend identifies Math in yellow and Code in blue. A red outlined star appears beside AZR (Ours), indicating the zero-data method in the page context. An orange label reading “457k” is aligned with PRIME-Zero. No other data-size marks are clearly visible. The Math Domain and Coding Domain panels each plot performance against Training Steps, with a blue trace and pale blue shaded area; both rise quickly at first, then fluctuate as they improve more gradually. Math starts near 0.25, reaches about 0.35 by roughly 50 steps, varies mostly around 0.34–0.36, and rises to about 0.39 near the end. Coding starts near 0.565, climbs to about 0.60 by roughly 100 steps, and then fluctuates around 0.60–0.62. The Overall Performance panel plots training steps from 0 to 350 and performance from about 0.40 to 0.52. Its blue training trace rises from about 0.40 to around 0.47 by 75–100 steps, then oscillates near 0.48–0.49, ending close to 0.50. The legend identifies an open blue circle as “Base model,” a red dashed horizontal line as “Prev.
